title: The super Keyword
summary: Master the super keyword in Java: invoking parent constructors, calling parent methods, and accessing shadowed parent fields with precision.
learningObjectives: Master the 3 distinct use cases of the super keyword: super(), super.method(), and super.field
Understand the strict rule: super() constructor calls MUST be the very first statement
Differentiate shadowed parent fields from child fields using super.fieldName
Contrast the super reference with the this reference in method and constructor scopes
expectedOutcomes: Ability to invoke parent behavior and constructors without compilation errors
Deep understanding of how super resolves shadowed members in the JVM

activities.title: The Satellite to Mission Control Analogy
activities.content:
Imagine an orbital satellite operating in deep space with its own local sensors and memory.

When the satellite makes an observation, it can either:
1. Look at its own local memory (`this.cameraReading`).
2. Or send an uplink to **Mission Control Headquarters** to request parent calibration telemetry (`super.calibratedBaseline`).
3. When booting up, the satellite MUST establish contact with Mission Control before initializing local sub-systems (`super(satelliteId)` as the very first operation).

The `super` keyword is that direct uplink to headquarters: it explicitly references the parent scope above the local object.

activities.title: The Three Powers of super: Constructors, Methods, and Fields
activities.content:
In Java, `super` is a reference variable used by a subclass to refer directly to its **immediate parent class**.

### 1. The Three Distinct Uses of `super`:

| Use Case | Syntax | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Constructor Call** | `super(...)` | Invokes the parent constructor. **MUST be the very first statement** in the subclass constructor. |
| **2. Method Call** | `super.methodName(...)` | Invokes the parent class implementation of a method. |
| **3. Field Access** | `super.fieldName` | Accesses a shadowed/hidden parent field when the child declares a field with the same name. |

### 2. Constructor Invocation Rules:
- If you write `super(args);`, it **must be on line 1** of the constructor body. You cannot write code before `super()`.
- You **cannot use both `this()` and `super()`** in the same constructor because both demand to be the first statement!
- If a subclass constructor does not explicitly call `super(...)` or `this(...)`, the Java compiler automatically inserts an implicit **`super();`** (calling the parent's zero-argument constructor).

### 3. Resolving Field Shadowing:
```java
class Parent {
    int speed = 50;
}
class Child extends Parent {
    int speed = 100; // Shadows Parent's speed
    void printSpeeds() {
        System.out.println(this.speed);  // Prints 100 (Child)
        System.out.println(super.speed); // Prints 50 (Parent)
    }
}
```

activities.title: Comprehensive Demonstration of super in Action
activities.description: Trace all three uses of super within a Vehicle and SportsCar hierarchy.

steps.description: super(vehicleSpeed) on line 1 invokes the Vehicle constructor first.
super.maxSpeed resolves the parent's field (140), while this.maxSpeed resolves the child's field (300).
super.displayStatus() explicitly calls the Vehicle superclass implementation.

activities.title: Example 2: Demonstrating the Line 1 Rule for super()
activities.description: Examine why placing statements before super() causes a compilation failure.

steps.description: The compiler rejects any statement before super() to ensure parent invariants are established first.
Once super() finishes, child-specific initialization logic runs safely.

activities.title: Mastery Verification: The super Keyword (10 Questions)

questions.question: What does the super keyword represent in Java?
options: A reference variable to the current object
A reference variable to the immediate parent class object scope
A global static pointer
A JVM garbage collector command
questions.explanation: super is a reference variable used by a subclass to refer directly to its immediate parent class.

questions.question: Where must an explicit call to super() be placed in a subclass constructor?
options: Anywhere in the constructor body
As the very first statement in the constructor
As the last statement before returning
Inside a synchronized block
questions.explanation: Java mandates that super() or this() must be the very first statement in a constructor.

questions.question: Can you use both this() and super() in the same constructor body?
options: Yes, in any order
No, because both demand to be the first statement of the constructor
Yes, if one of them is empty
Only in private constructors
questions.explanation: Both this() and super() require being on the first line; therefore, they can never coexist in the same constructor.

questions.question: What happens if a subclass constructor does NOT explicitly write super() or this()?
options: The program will not compile
The compiler automatically inserts an implicit 'super();' call on line 1
The parent constructor is never executed
The object is marked corrupt in the heap
questions.explanation: The Java compiler automatically inserts an implicit zero-argument 'super();' call.

questions.question: What happens if the parent class has NO zero-argument constructor, and the subclass does not write an explicit super(args)?
options: The compiler creates a fake 0-arg constructor in the parent
Compile-time error: constructor Parent() is undefined
Runtime NullPointerException
All parent fields become 0
questions.explanation: If no default constructor exists in the parent, the compiler's implicit 'super();' fails, producing a compile-time error.

questions.question: Can the super keyword be used inside a static method?
options: Yes, to access static parent methods
No, super cannot be used in a static context because static methods have no instance ('this')
Only if the superclass is abstract
Only in Java 21
questions.explanation: Static methods belong to the class, not an instance. Using 'super' in a static context causes a compile-time error.

questions.question: How can a subclass access a parent method that has the same name as a method in the subclass?
options: this.methodName()
super.methodName()
Parent.methodName()
parent::methodName()
questions.explanation: 'super.methodName()' invokes the parent class implementation explicitly.

questions.question: If class Parent has field 'int value = 10' and class Child has field 'int value = 20', what does 'super.value' print inside Child?
options: Compilation error due to duplicate variable
questions.explanation: 'super.value' references the shadowed parent field, accessing 10.

questions.question: Can you write 'super.super.method()' to bypass the direct parent and invoke a grandparent method?
options: Yes, it is standard Java syntax
No, super.super is strictly illegal in Java
Only if parent is package-private
Only if grandparent is Object
questions.explanation: Java prohibits 'super.super' to enforce parent encapsulation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid use of the super keyword?
options: Invoking a parent constructor: super(arg1, arg2)
Invoking an overridden parent method: super.render()
Accessing a shadowed parent variable: super.taxRate
Declaring a new class: class Child super Parent { }
questions.explanation: Classes use the 'extends' keyword to inherit, not 'super'.

interviewQA.question: What are the three distinct uses of the super keyword in Java?
interviewQA.answer: 1. Invoking parent constructors via 'super(arguments)'. 2. Invoking parent methods via 'super.methodName()'. 3. Accessing shadowed parent fields via 'super.fieldName'.

interviewQA.question: Why does Java mandate that super() must be the very first statement in a constructor?
interviewQA.answer: A child class inherits and depends on the fields and invariants of its parent class. If child code could execute before the parent constructor, the child could read uninitialized or invalid parent state. Establishing parent invariants first ensures object integrity and memory safety.

interviewQA.question: What occurs if a superclass does not define a default zero-argument constructor?
interviewQA.answer: If a superclass defines parameterized constructors and omits a 0-arg constructor, any subclass must explicitly invoke one of the available parent constructors using 'super(arg1, arg2)' on line 1. Otherwise, the compiler attempts to insert an implicit 'super();', which fails compilation.

interviewQA.question: Can you use the super keyword in static methods or static blocks? Why or why not?
interviewQA.answer: No. The 'super' keyword relies on an active object instance on the heap to determine the parent scope. Because static methods belong to the class template and execute without any 'this' instance context, referencing 'super' in a static context raises a compile-time error.

interviewQA.question: What is field shadowing and how does super resolve it?
interviewQA.answer: Field shadowing occurs when a subclass declares a field with the exact same name as a field in its superclass. Both fields exist in memory. By default, unqualified variable access resolves to the child field. The child can use 'super.fieldName' to explicitly read or write the parent's shadowed field.

interviewQA.question: Why does Java disallow 'super.super' syntax?
interviewQA.answer: Allowing 'super.super' would violate object-oriented encapsulation. A subclass should only interact with its immediate contract (the direct parent). If a parent class overrides a grandparent method to enforce validation or security, bypassing the parent via 'super.super' would compromise system invariants.

activities.title: Module 5 Lesson 9 Mastery Checkpoint
checklist: I know the 3 distinct use cases of the super keyword
I understand why super() must be the very first statement in a constructor
I know that this() and super() cannot coexist in the same constructor
I know that the compiler inserts an implicit super() if none is written
I can diagnose compile errors when a parent lacks a zero-argument constructor
I know why super cannot be used in static methods
I can resolve shadowed parent fields using super.fieldName
I can invoke parent method implementations using super.methodName()
I understand why super.super is strictly forbidden in Java
I can trace constructor chaining and member resolution in complex class hierarchies

practiceProblems.title: Warmup: Use super() to Initialize Parent Person State
practiceProblems.description: Invoke the parent constructor using super(name, age) in the Employee subclass.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Class Person has fields name and age with a constructor Person(String name, int age). Implement Employee extending Person, using super(name, age) on line 1, and adding employeeId (String).
hints: Employee constructor must call super(name, age) on line 1.
display() prints formatted string matching expected output.

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Resolving Shadowed Field with super.field
practiceProblems.description: Demonstrate shadowed field resolution where both parent and child declare double interestRate.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Create BankAccount with protected double interestRate = 3.0. Create PremiumAccount extending BankAccount with protected double interestRate = 6.5. In PremiumAccount, write compareRates() printing both super.interestRate and this.interestRate. From scratch.

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Calling Parent Method Implementation with super.method()
practiceProblems.description: Augment parent calculation logic by calling super.calculatePrice() before applying luxury tax.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Build Product with calculatePrice(double baseCost) returning baseCost * 1.10 (10% standard tax). Build LuxuryProduct extending Product with calculatePrice(double baseCost) which calls super.calculatePrice(baseCost) and adds $500 luxury surcharge. From scratch.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Broken Code: super() Not First Statement
practiceProblems.description: Fix a compilation failure caused by placing a print statement before super().
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The code fails to compile with 'constructor call must be the first statement in a constructor'. Fix the constructor by moving super(brand) to line 1.
hints: super(brand) must be the first line of Microwave constructor.

practiceProblems.title: Challenge: Multi-Stage Order Processing with super Delegation
practiceProblems.description: Build an EnterpriseOrder processor where Subclass validates customs clearance before delegating to super.processOrder().
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Create Order with orderId (String), amount (double), and processOrder() returning amount. Create InternationalOrder extending Order with destinationCountry (String), customsDutyRate (double), and processOrder() calling super.processOrder() and adding (amount * customsDutyRate / 100.0).
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Order ORD-998 Base Processed: $2000.0
International Order ORD-998 [Destination: Germany] Total with Customs: $2300.0
hints: In InternationalOrder.processOrder(), call super.processOrder() + customs duty.
